title: The Root Edit Primitive is non-operational until a Prime Agent attains Independent Governance
content:
A.2.2.6.2.3.1 suspends the mechanism the whole Section defines: "Until a Prime Agent has Independent Governance, the Root Edit Primitive will not be operational. Instead, if a Prime Agent wishes to edit its Agent Artifact, it must use the customary Atlas Edit Proposal processes" — the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle or Monthly Cycle.

This is the second suspension of the same kind in this Article, after Founder Access (A.2.2.1.1.3.2.1), and both redirect to the same fallback. The result is that at present *no* stage of an Agent's life uses the Agent-specific editing mechanisms the Atlas specifies: pre-Transformation edits go through Atlas Edit cycles because Founder Access is off, and post-Root-Edit edits go through Atlas Edit cycles because Root Edit is off.

The gating condition is worth noting — Independent Governance (A.0.1.1.54), a status an Agent attains rather than a date. So the suspension is not a scheduled rollout but a per-Agent capability gate, and Agents will migrate off the fallback path at different times.

The practical consequence is a load transfer. Every Prime Agent's internal governance decisions become items in Sky's own weekly cycle, competing with ecosystem-level business, and Agent token holders' votes are replaced by SKY holders' votes for the duration.
description: Until then a Prime cannot use its own governance process at all and must amend its Artifact through the ecosystem-wide Atlas Edit Weekly or Monthly Cycle instead.
